title: Pseudo-SD: Pseudo Controlled Stable Diffusion for Semi-Supervised and Cross-Domain Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion on (unlabelled/target image, pseudo-label, text) triples with partial attention manipulation and structured pseudo-labels. Then generate label-controlled synthetic images in the target style and train the segmenter on them.
adaptation: Fine-tune a mask-conditioned SD on the 1,152 pool half-cells with their pseudo-labels, then render half-cut cells from labelled inactive and crack layouts. SD smears 1-2 px lines, so use the generated cells for inactive and layout context, and paste real crack pixels back.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + 2k generated half-cut cells, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: E1 inactive IoU and crack relF1@2, clean-49 non-inferiority. Kill: E1 inactive IoU < PF + 0.03 and E1 crack relF1@2 < PF + 0.02.
evidence: R: new state of the art on semi-supervised and cross-domain segmentation benchmarks when injected into current methods (numbers not retrieved).
prior_overlap: None. Generative synthesis is untested. Synthetic half-cut views made by geometry were n.d., but that is a different mechanism.
